answer: A work-history vine limits sybil damage: each identity carries a public chain of graded tasks, and new identities must post a ferrous bond, hard stake forfeited on verified misbehavior. Reputation is non-transferable, so cloned accounts restart at zero trust and each needs its own bond. A cheap passive signal, such as peer-signed uptime heartbeats, flags clones reusing identical model weights. At scale the attacker stakes N bonds while earning nothing until each vine matures, so cost grows linearly and benefit stays near zero.
